messages:
anya: fyi nightly eval on rwd/xl-quant-v2 shows a cluster of prompt-set timeouts. tests that passed yesterday are timing out now :eyes:
anya: nightly job link: https://ci.redwood.ai/teams/eng-ml/runs/4521 — failures start around 1713467000
kevin: any stack traces? most timeouts have been worker-process hangs or ordering issues lately
ci-bot: Job 4521 failed 12/120 tests, artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/4521/logs.tar.gz :robot_face:
chris: skimmed the logs — generator worker waits on a prompt slot. debug trace shows request ordering different from reference ordering (same inputs, permuted order)
natalie: note we switched prompt dedup sorting from sha1 -> murmur3 in eval harness (PR #289) last week. murmur3 is deterministic but our vendored impl is 32-bit and may have platform-dependent tie behavior
anya: the diffs from yesterday show ~8 prompts permuted; that reshuffle can change KV-cache warmup and lead to later timeouts on long-context tests
kevin: can you paste a tiny repro? I can try running with sha1 fallback to confirm
natalie: quick repro below — shows different sort orders for murmur vs sha1
```
# order-diff.py
from pathlib import Path
from eval_harness.hashing import murmur_hash, sha1_hash
prompts = [f'p{i}' for i in range(100)]
print(sorted(prompts, key=lambda p: murmur_hash(p) % 100))
print(sorted(prompts, key=lambda p: sha1_hash(p)))
```
natalie: locally murmur-based sort permutes a handful of items compared to sha1. more worrying: our murmur impl used little-endian reads and produced tie orders that vary across CI nodes
chris: that would explain cross-node flakiness. mitigation: revert ordering to sha1 OR use a stable tie-breaker (hash, original_index) for deterministic sort
anya: short-term mitigation: bump per-test timeout to 90s for affected prompt-set and mark it flaky in nightly metadata. i'll open a hotfix to pin ordering
kevin: opened PR #304 to add stable_sort wrapper and unit tests. assigning natalie for review
natalie: reviewing now. adding a stress test that runs 1k randomized inputs across both hashing impls to catch endian/tie cases
ci-bot: PR #304 pipeline started — build 783 passed unit tests, integration flaky on infra agent
anya: thanks — we'll monitor the next 3 nightly runs and roll back the mitigation if green. adding note to release notes and postmortem if it recurs
kevin: sha1 fallback should be slightly slower but negligible compared to timeout risk. :thumbsup:
anya: ok closing once we get two consecutive green nightlies
